question: What does Qnami do currently? Summarise it in 200 words
answer:
Here’s a 200‑word summary of what Qnami currently does:

Qnami is a Swiss venture‑capital‑backed deep‑tech company, founded in 2017 and headquartered in Muttenz, Switzerland, that specializes in quantum sensing technologies ([linkedin.com](https://www.linkedin.com/company/qnami/?utm_source=openai)). The company develops and commercializes advanced quantum microscopes—most notably the ProteusQ™, the world’s first commercial Scanning NV (nitrogen‑vacancy) magnetometer, which uses diamond‑based Quantilever™ probes to map magnetic fields at the nanoscale ([thequantuminsider.com](https://thequantuminsider.com/2021/05/12/swiss-based-qnami-closes-4-million-chf-4-4-million-u-s-series-a-funding-round/?utm_source=openai)).

Qnami’s instruments are used in materials science, spintronics, life sciences, and navigation, enabling researchers to visualize magnetic and electronic properties with unprecedented precision ([thequantuminsider.com](https://thequantuminsider.com/2024/02/02/qnami-expands-into-japan-and-south-korea/?utm_source=openai)). The company continues to expand its global reach through strategic distribution partnerships: it collaborates with Quantum Design in the U.S., and has exclusive distribution agreements in Japan and South Korea via Quantum Design’s regional subsidiaries ([thequantuminsider.com](https://thequantuminsider.com/2024/02/02/qnami-expands-into-japan-and-south-korea/?utm_source=openai)).

In Europe, Qnami supports semiconductor innovation—such as aiding VerticalCompute in developing next‑generation, energy‑efficient chiplets—by providing its quantum metrology solutions ([qnami.ch](https://qnami.ch/qnami-supports-verticalcompute-driving-european-semiconductor-innovation/?utm_source=openai)). Overall, Qnami bridges cutting‑edge quantum sensing research and industrial applications, delivering high‑precision tools for nanoscale imaging and characterization.
